title: (No AI) Wildwood’s director says AI is ‘antithetical to everything that we are at this studio’
author: Andrew Webster
content:
![A still from the stop-motion film Wildwood showing a child with glasses in a tall military-style hat next to a woman in armor.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/WILDWOOD-Curtis-Alexandra-Still-Credit_-LAIKA.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

_Wildwood_ is the most ambitious film yet from Laika, the stop-motion studio best known for the likes of _Coraline_ and _ParaNorman_. It's a sprawling fantasy adventure that took five years to complete. The process involved more 230 puppets - including 36 of the main character Prue alone - which were brought to life by a team of 49 animators. All told, more than 1,000 artists worked on the film in some form. The painstaking process that goes into making a Laika film offers a distinct counterpoint to the instant progress promised by generative AI tools.

Recently _Wildwood_ director and Laika CEO [Travis Knight joined](https://www.reddit.com/r/antiai/comments/1xbiclk/wildwood_director_travis_knight_says_ai_is_not_a/) [a chorus](https://deadline.com/2025/10/guillermo-del-toro-would-rather-die-than-use-generative-ai-1236597071/) [of influencer](https://www.ign.com/articles/f-ai-star-wars-and-knives-out-director-rian-johnson-blasts-ai-as-making-everything-worse-in-every-single-way) [filmmakers](https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/jul/13/christopher-nolan-odyssey-director-comments-ai-artificial-intelligence) …

[Read the full story at The Verge.](https://www.theverge.com/entertainment/1016647/wildwood-travis-knight-interview-ai-laika-stop-motion)

title: (No AI) OpenAI, Anthropic, and Nvidia had record lobbying quarters
author: Lauren Feiner
content:
![Capitol Hill](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2025/09/STK481_STK432_CONGRESS_GOVERNMENT_CIVRGINIA_C.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

It was a busy summer for AI lobbyists. Anthropic, OpenAI, and Nvidia each had their highest-spending lobbying quarter between July and September, federal disclosures show.

Nvidia spent the most of the group at $2.2 million, followed by Anthropic's $2.1 million and OpenAI's $1.5 million. Compared to other Big Tech companies with long-established presences in Washington, the sums aren't out of the ordinary. Microsoft, for example, has spent at least $2 million a quarter going back to 2021, and Google regularly spends over $3 million, including this quarter. But it's a clear signal that the three AI firms recognize how important shaping policy …

[Read the full story at The Verge.](https://www.theverge.com/policy/1016585/openai-anthropic-nvidia-lobbying-records)
